title: Find the Percent of a Number
contentObjective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words percent, base, part, and equation.

noticeAndWonder.context: Before we head to Discount Day at the arcade, warm up with a percent of a number. This storage bar shows part of a whole, just like a percent-off deal shows part of a ticket price. Approximately what percent of the storage is used? If the phone holds 200 GB, about how many gigabytes is that percent of the whole?
noticeStarters: I notice about ___% of the storage bar is used, because the filled part is ___ the halfway mark.
I notice the base is 200 GB, so 1% would be ___ GB.
I notice ___% used means ___ out of every 100 GB.
wonderStarters: I wonder how many GB ___% of 200 GB works out to.
I wonder whether 10% of 200 GB helps me estimate ___%.
I wonder what percent would be used if ___ GB were full instead.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Food Drive
revealWordProblem.text: The organizers of a food drive set a new goal for a second food drive. They hope to collect 140% as many cans as they did for the last food drive in which they collected 145 cans. About how many cans can the organizers expect to collect? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Change 140% to its decimal form: 140% = 1.40. Multiply the decimal by the base: 1.40 × 145 = 203. The organizers can expect to collect about 203 cans for the second food drive.

turnAndTalk.question: On Discount Day the claw machine is 25% off its 60-ticket price. In '25% of 60,' which number is the base (the number right after 'of'), and what part are you trying to find?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The base is 60 — it comes right after 'of' — and the part is the discount, 25% of 60.

stems.en: The base is ___ and the part I want is ___.
stems.es: La base es ___ y la parte que quiero es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students identify 60 as the base, the 25% discount as the part to find, and connect 'of' to the base.
turnAndTalk.extend: Without computing exactly, will the discount be more or less than half of 60? Use a benchmark to estimate and explain.
extendStems: The discount will be ___ than half because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: What steps did you follow every time to find the percent of a number in the discount table?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I changed the percent to a decimal, then multiplied it by the base to get the part.
turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students describe the equation part = percent x base, converting the percent to a decimal first (e.g., 0.40 x 80 = 32).
turnAndTalk.extend: Compare finding 25% of 60 with the decimal 0.25 versus dividing 60 into 4 equal parts. Why do both methods give the same part?
extendStems: Both give ___ because 25% is the same as ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The arcade donates 12% of Saturday's 1,500 ticket sales. The manager says 180 tickets, a student says 18. Who is right, and how do you know?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 12% of 1,500 is 0.12 times 1,500, which is 180 tickets.

stems.en: The ___ is correct because 12% of 1,500 = ___ x 1,500 = ___.
stems.es: El/La ___ tiene razón porque 12% de 1,500 = ___ x 1,500 = ___.

stems.en: The mistake was using ___ instead of ___.
stems.es: El error fue usar ___ en lugar de ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute 0.12 x 1,500 = 180 and explain the student likely used 0.012 (divided by 1,000) instead of 0.12.
turnAndTalk.extend: Estimate first: 10% of 1,500 is easy to find. Use that to check whether 180 is reasonable for 12%, and explain your reasoning.
extendStems: 10% of 1,500 is ___, so 12% should be a little ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Find the Percent of a Number, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: To find the part, change the percent to a decimal, then multiply: part = percent × base.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.4 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: A part of a number found by multiplying the number by the percent written as a decimal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una parte de un número que se halla multiplicando el número por el porcentaje escrito como decimal.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A number out of 100 is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: The number you take the percent OF — it is the number right after the word 'of'.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del que sacas el porcentaje — es el número que va después de la palabra 'de'.
vocabulary.visual: In '25% of 80,' the base is 80. In '140% of 145,' the base is still 145.
vocabulary.cloze: The number right after the word 'of' in a percent problem is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: The amount the percent gives you — the answer to percent × base.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que te da el porcentaje — el resultado de porcentaje × base.
vocabulary.visual: 25% of 80 = 20, so the part is 20. 140% of 145 = 203, so the part is 203.
vocabulary.cloze: The amount you get after you multiply percent × base is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign showing both sides are the same.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con un signo igual que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: A math sentence with an equal sign, like part = percent × base, is an ___.

vocabulary.definition: Money taken off the first price to make it cheaper.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dinero que se quita del precio original para que sea más barato.
vocabulary.cloze: An amount subtracted from a price is a ___.

visual.title: Discount Day: Two Arcade Deals
visual.caption: Which game's deal shades off a bigger slice of its full price — and about how much of the whole bar is that?

launch.narrative: It's Discount Day at the arcade! Different games are offering percent-off deals on ticket prices. The claw machine is 25% off its usual 60-ticket price, and the racing game is 40% off 80 tickets. You need to calculate the discounts to figure out how many tickets each game actually costs!
launch.contextImage: Arcade games with colorful discount signs showing various percent-off deals
noticePrompts: What information do you need to find the discount amount?
How is finding 25% of 60 different from finding 40% of 80?
wonderPrompts: Is there more than one way to find a percent of a number?
How does a bar model help you see the percent of a number?

conceptIntro.heading: How do I find the percent of a number?
conceptIntro.intro: The base is the number right after the word "of" — and that word "of" is telling you to multiply. The part is the amount you end up with.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To find the part, change the percent to a decimal, then multiply: part = percent × base.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: The claw machine is 25% off its 60-ticket price. I want the discount.
First I change 25% to a decimal: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25.
Then I multiply by the base: 0.25 × 60 = 15.
So the discount is 15 tickets. The part is 15.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's find 40% of 80. What is 40% as a decimal? (0.40)

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the table, change each percent to a decimal, then multiply by the base.
Find the discount amount for each arcade game.

explore.instructions: Find the percent of each number. Use the equation: Part = Percent × Base. Convert the percent to a decimal first.

discourse.prompt: What steps do you follow every time you find the percent of a number?
discourse.sentenceFrame: To find ___% of ___, I first convert the percent to ___, then I multiply ___ × ___ = ___.

optional.stem: The claw machine prize is 80 tickets and today it is 25% off. How many tickets do you save?
choiceFeedback: Find 25% of 80, then subtract from 80.
Did you find the discount amount and subtract correctly?
Check: 25% of 80 is how much off?
optional.stemEs: El premio de la máquina de garra cuesta 80 boletos y hoy tiene 25% de descuento. ¿Cuántos boletos ahorras?
hints: A percent is a part out of 100, and 25% means one quarter of the whole.
The 80 tickets are the whole. Rewrite 25% as the decimal 0.25 and multiply, or split 80 into four equal parts.
Set up 0.25 × 80 and multiply — or divide 80 into 4 equal groups and take one group.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje es una parte de 100, y 25% significa una cuarta parte del entero.
Los 80 boletos son el entero. Escribe 25% como el decimal 0.25 y multiplica, o divide 80 en cuatro partes iguales.
Plantea 0.25 × 80 y multiplica, o divide 80 en 4 grupos iguales y toma un grupo.

optional.stem: Your bowling score was 60 points. The bonus round adds 15% more points. How many bonus points is that?
choiceFeedback: Find 15% of 60, then add to the original score.
Did you add the bonus to the original correctly?
Check: 15% of 60 is how much bonus?
optional.stemEs: Tu puntaje de boliche fue de 60 puntos. La ronda de bonificación agrega 15% más de puntos. ¿Cuántos puntos de bonificación son?
hints: The bonus is a percent of the score you already earned, so 60 is the whole.
Turn 15% into the decimal 0.15 and multiply — or find 10% first and then half of that for the extra 5%.
10% of 60 is 6, and 5% is half of that amount. Put those two pieces together to get the bonus.
hintsEs: La bonificación es un porcentaje del puntaje que ya ganaste, así que 60 es el entero.
Convierte 15% en el decimal 0.15 y multiplica, o halla primero el 10% y luego la mitad de eso para el 5% extra.
El 10% de 60 es 6, y el 5% es la mitad de esa cantidad. Junta esas dos partes para obtener la bonificación.

optional.stem: A snack at the arcade costs $40. The sales tax is 5%. How many dollars is the tax?
choiceFeedback: Find 5% of $40, then add to the original price.
Did you include both the price and the tax?
Check: 5% of $40 is how much tax?
optional.stemEs: Un refrigerio en el arcade cuesta $40. El impuesto sobre la venta es del 5%. ¿Cuántos dólares es el impuesto?
hints: Sales tax is a percent of the price, so the $40 is the whole.
Rewrite 5% as the decimal 0.05 and multiply it by the price.
Set up 0.05 × 40 and multiply. If the decimal feels tricky, find 10% of $40 first and then take half of it.
hintsEs: El impuesto sobre la venta es un porcentaje del precio, así que los $40 son el entero.
Escribe 5% como el decimal 0.05 y multiplícalo por el precio.
Plantea 0.05 × 40 y multiplica. Si el decimal te cuesta, halla primero el 10% de $40 y luego toma la mitad.

optional.label: Match each percent-of-a-number tip to its result.
optional.explanation: Each tip is the percent written as a decimal times its base: 0.20 × 70 = 14, 0.50 × 46 = 23, 0.10 × 90 = 9, and 0.30 × 200 = 60. Friendly shortcuts confirm them fast — 50% is just half, and 10% slides the decimal one place left.
optional.explanationEs: Cada propina es el porcentaje escrito como decimal por su base: 0.20 × 70 = 14, 0.50 × 46 = 23, 0.10 × 90 = 9 y 0.30 × 200 = 60. Los atajos fáciles los confirman rápido: 50% es simplemente la mitad, y 10% mueve el punto decimal un lugar a la izquierda.
hints: Every card asks for a part of a base, so each answer must be smaller than the number after the word 'of'.
Change the percent to a decimal and multiply, or use shortcuts: 50% is half, and 10% moves the decimal one place left.
Start with 10% of 90: slide the decimal in 90 one place left. That single match rules out one card and shrinks the board.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta pide una parte de una base, así que cada respuesta debe ser menor que el número que sigue a la palabra 'de'.
Cambia el porcentaje a decimal y multiplica, o usa atajos: 50% es la mitad y 10% mueve el punto decimal un lugar a la izquierda.
Empieza con 10% de 90: mueve el punto decimal de 90 un lugar a la izquierda. Esa sola pareja descarta una tarjeta y reduce el tablero.
optional.labelEs: Une cada consejo de porcentaje de un número con su resultado.

optional.instructions: Each arcade game shows a percent of a number. Sort each one into the correct result bin.
optional.explanation: Working out each card sorts it: 0.25 × 48 = 12 and 0.40 × 30 = 12 land in the Equals 12 bin, while 0.75 × 40 = 30 and 0.10 × 300 = 30 land in Equals 30. Notice that '40% of 30' and '75% of 40' use the same two numbers but give different results, so you have to compute rather than pattern-match.
optional.explanationEs: Al resolver cada tarjeta se decide su lugar: 0.25 × 48 = 12 y 0.40 × 30 = 12 caen en la casilla Igual a 12, mientras que 0.75 × 40 = 30 y 0.10 × 300 = 30 caen en Igual a 30. Fíjate en que '40% de 30' y '75% de 40' usan los mismos dos números pero dan resultados distintos, así que hay que calcular en vez de adivinar por el patrón.
hints: There are only two possible results here, 12 and 30, so each card just needs to be worked out and compared.
Turn the percent into a decimal and multiply by the number after 'of', or use fraction shortcuts like 25% = 1/4 and 75% = 3/4.
Start with '25% of 48': that is 48 ÷ 4. Compute it and see which bin the card belongs in, then do the same for the rest.
hintsEs: Aquí solo hay dos resultados posibles, 12 y 30, así que cada tarjeta solo hay que resolverla y compararla.
Convierte el porcentaje en decimal y multiplica por el número que sigue a 'de', o usa atajos con fracciones como 25% = 1/4 y 75% = 3/4.
Empieza con '25% de 48': eso es 48 ÷ 4. Calcúlalo y mira a qué casilla va la tarjeta, y luego haz lo mismo con las demás.
optional.instructionsEs: Cada juego del arcade muestra un porcentaje de un número. Clasifica cada uno en el grupo de resultados correcto.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Discount Dash Color-by-Code Error
optional.correctWork: First change 20% to a decimal: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20. Then multiply by the base: 0.20 × 50 = 10. So 20% of 50 = 10, not 20.
hints: A percent is not a whole number by itself — change 20% to a decimal before you multiply.
20% = 0.20. Then multiply 0.20 × 50 to find the part.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Error del código de color de Discount Dash
optional.explanation: The work never uses the base at all: it takes 20 straight from '20%' and calls that the part. Percent means per hundred, so 20% = 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20, and the part is 0.20 × 50 = 10.
optional.explanationEs: El trabajo nunca usa la base: toma el 20 directamente de '20%' y lo llama la parte. Por ciento significa por cada cien, así que 20% = 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20, y la parte es 0.20 × 50 = 10.

choiceFeedback: Multiply 150 by 0.20, or divide by 5.
Double-check your multiplication.
Try converting 20% to a decimal or fraction first.
hints: '20% of 150' means you want a PART of 150 — the answer should be smaller than 150.
Convert the percent to a decimal, then multiply: Part = Percent × Base.
Write 20% as 0.20, then set up 0.20 × 150. (Shortcut: 10% of 150 is 15 — double it.)
hintsEs: '20% de 150' significa que quieres una PARTE de 150: la respuesta debe ser menor que 150.
Convierte el porcentaje en decimal y luego multiplica: Parte = Porcentaje × Base.
Escribe 20% como 0.20 y plantea 0.20 × 150. (Atajo: 10% de 150 es 15; duplícalo.)

choiceFeedback: 50% is half — divide 84 by 2.
Check your calculation.
Remember: 50% means one-half.
hints: 50% is a friendly percent — it means exactly one-half of the number.
Finding 50% of a number is the same as dividing that number by 2.
Set up 84 ÷ 2, or check with the formula: 0.50 × 84.
hintsEs: 50% es un porcentaje amigable: significa exactamente la mitad del número.
Hallar el 50% de un número es lo mismo que dividir ese número entre 2.
Plantea 84 ÷ 2, o compruébalo con la fórmula: 0.50 × 84.

approaching.explanation: 10% = 0.10. Multiply: 0.10 × 320 = 32. (Or move the decimal one place left.)
choiceFeedback: 10% is one-tenth — divide 320 by 10 or move the decimal.
Check: what is one-tenth of 320?
10% is easy: just divide by 10.
hints: 10% means one-tenth — there's a shortcut that needs no multiplication at all.
To find 10% of any number, move the decimal point one place to the left (divide by 10).
Start with 320 and slide the decimal one place left: 320 → what number?
approaching.explanationEs: 10% = 0.10. Multiplica: 0.10 × 320 = 32. (O mueve el punto decimal un lugar a la izquierda.)
hintsEs: 10% significa un décimo: hay un atajo que no necesita ninguna multiplicación.
Para hallar el 10% de cualquier número, mueve el punto decimal un lugar a la izquierda (divide entre 10).
Empieza con 320 y desliza el punto un lugar a la izquierda: 320 → ¿qué número?

choiceFeedback: Divide 15 by 50, then multiply by 100.
Set it up as a fraction: 15/50, then convert to a percent.
Find what fraction 15 is of 50, then convert.
hints: This question is backwards from the others: you have the part (15) and the whole (50), and you need the PERCENT.
Write the part over the whole as a fraction, then convert that fraction to a percent.
Set up 15/50. Divide 15 by 50 to get a decimal, then multiply by 100.
hintsEs: Esta pregunta va al revés de las otras: tienes la parte (15) y el todo (50), y necesitas el PORCENTAJE.
Escribe la parte sobre el todo como fracción y luego convierte esa fracción en porcentaje.
Plantea 15/50. Divide 15 entre 50 para obtener un decimal y luego multiplica por 100.

approaching.instructions: Find each percent of a number using the formula: Part = Percent × Base.
hints: The finished row shows the recipe: 25% of 60 became 0.25 × 60 = 15. Your rows use the same formula.
Convert each percent to a decimal, then multiply by the Base: Part = Percent × Base.
Row 2: write 40% as 0.40 and multiply 0.40 × 80. Then do 0.15 × 200 for the last row.
approaching.explanation: Part = Percent × Base works once the percent is written as a decimal, exactly as the finished row shows with 0.25 × 60 = 15. So 40% of 80 is 0.40 × 80 = 32, and 15% of 200 is 0.15 × 200 = 30.
approaching.explanationEs: Parte = Porcentaje × Base funciona una vez que el porcentaje se escribe como decimal, tal como muestra la fila ya resuelta con 0.25 × 60 = 15. Entonces 40% de 80 es 0.40 × 80 = 32, y 15% de 200 es 0.15 × 200 = 30.
approaching.instructionsEs: Encuentra cada porcentaje de un número con la fórmula: Parte = Porcentaje × Base.
hintsEs: La fila terminada muestra la receta: 25% de 60 se volvió 0.25 × 60 = 15. Tus filas usan la misma fórmula.
Convierte cada porcentaje en decimal y luego multiplica por la Base: Parte = Porcentaje × Base.
Fila 2: escribe 40% como 0.40 y multiplica 0.40 × 80. Luego haz 0.15 × 200 para la última fila.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: First change the percent to a decimal: 30% = 30 ÷ 100 = 0.30. Then multiply by the base: 0.30 × 80 = 24. So 30% of 80 = 24, not 2,400. The student multiplied by 30 instead of 0.30.
hints: A percent is not a whole number — change 30% to a decimal before you multiply.
30% = 0.30. Multiply 0.30 × 80 to find the part: 24.
approaching.explanation: The student multiplied by 30 instead of by 30%. Percent means per hundred, so 30% = 30 ÷ 100 = 0.30, and 0.30 × 80 = 24. An answer of 2,400 should also look wrong right away, since a part of 80 can never be larger than 80.
approaching.explanationEs: El estudiante multiplicó por 30 en vez de por 30%. Por ciento significa por cada cien, así que 30% = 30 ÷ 100 = 0.30, y 0.30 × 80 = 24. Una respuesta de 2,400 también debería verse mal de inmediato, porque una parte de 80 nunca puede ser mayor que 80.

onLevel.instructions: Complete each row to find the percent of a number.
hints: Every row is the same job: find the percent OF the base. The Part should be smaller than the Base when the percent is under 100%.
Convert each percent to a decimal and multiply by the base. Shortcut: find 10% first, then scale.
Row 1: 10% of 250 — slide the decimal in 250 one place left. For 75% of 120, try 0.75 × 120 (or 3/4 of 120).
onLevel.explanation: Each row is percent × base with the percent written as a decimal: 0.10 × 250 = 25, 0.75 × 120 = 90, 0.35 × 200 = 70, and 0.08 × 50 = 4. Every part comes out smaller than its base because each percent is under 100%.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada fila es porcentaje × base con el porcentaje escrito como decimal: 0.10 × 250 = 25, 0.75 × 120 = 90, 0.35 × 200 = 70 y 0.08 × 50 = 4. Cada parte resulta menor que su base porque cada porcentaje es menor que 100%.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Completa cada fila para encontrar el porcentaje de un número.
hintsEs: Cada fila es el mismo trabajo: hallar el porcentaje DE la base. La Parte debe ser menor que la Base cuando el porcentaje es menor de 100%.
Convierte cada porcentaje en decimal y multiplica por la base. Atajo: halla primero el 10% y luego escala.
Fila 1: 10% de 250 — desliza el punto de 250 un lugar a la izquierda. Para 75% de 120, prueba 0.75 × 120 (o 3/4 de 120).

onLevel.stem: An arcade prize costs 240 tickets. If you have a coupon for 15% off, how many tickets do you save?
choiceFeedback: Find the discount amount, then subtract from the original.
Make sure you're subtracting the discount from the total.
Check: what is the discount, and what's left?
hints: Read carefully: the question asks how many tickets you SAVE — that's just the discount amount, not the new price.
The savings = 15% of the original 240 tickets. Convert 15% to a decimal and multiply.
Set up 0.15 × 240. (Shortcut: 10% of 240 is 24, and 5% is half of that — add them.)
onLevel.stemEs: Un premio del arcade cuesta 240 boletos. Si tienes un cupón de 15% de descuento, ¿cuántos boletos ahorras?
hintsEs: Lee con cuidado: la pregunta es cuántos boletos AHORRAS, o sea solo el descuento, no el precio nuevo.
El ahorro es el 15% de los 240 boletos originales. Convierte 15% en decimal y multiplica.
Plantea 0.15 × 240. (Atajo: 10% de 240 es 24 y 5% es la mitad de eso; súmalos.)

onLevel.instructions: A game has 200 total points. Use the bar model to find 25% of 200.
onLevel.label: 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Each 25% section = 50 points. So 25% of 200 = 50.
hints: The bar shows 200 points cut into 4 equal sections, and each section is 25%.
Since 4 equal parts make the whole, one part = the whole divided by 4.
Divide 200 by 4 to find the value of one 25% section — that section IS 25% of 200.
onLevel.explanation: The bar cuts the 200 points into 4 equal sections, and 4 sections of 25% make 100%, so one section is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 points. That single section is exactly 25% of 200, so 25% of 200 = 50.
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra corta los 200 puntos en 4 secciones iguales, y 4 secciones de 25% forman 100%, así que una sección es 200 ÷ 4 = 50 puntos. Esa sección es exactamente 25% de 200, así que 25% de 200 = 50.

onLevel.stem: A student scored 72 out of 90 on a test. What percent did they score?
choiceFeedback: Divide 72 by 90, then multiply by 100.
Convert to a fraction first: 72/90, then to a percent.
Find what fraction 72 is of 90, then convert to percent.
hints: The score 72 is the part and 90 is the whole — you need what percent 72 is OF 90.
Divide the part by the whole, then multiply the decimal by 100 to get the percent.
Set up 72 ÷ 90. (It may help to simplify 72/90 first — both divide by 9.)
onLevel.stemEs: Un estudiante obtuvo 72 de 90 en un examen. ¿Qué porcentaje obtuvo?
hintsEs: La calificación 72 es la parte y 90 es el todo: necesitas qué porcentaje es 72 DE 90.
Divide la parte entre el todo y luego multiplica el decimal por 100 para obtener el porcentaje.
Plantea 72 ÷ 90. (Puede ayudar simplificar 72/90 primero: ambos se dividen entre 9.)

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Change the percent to a decimal

onLevel.correctWork: The base is 60, not 15. The word "of" tells you the base: 15% OF 60. Multiply by the base: 0.15 × 60 = 9. So 15% of 60 = 9, not 2.25. The student multiplied by the percent number instead of the base.
hints: What number comes after the word "of"? That is the base you multiply by.
15% = 0.15, and the base is 60. Multiply 0.15 × 60 = 9.
onLevel.explanation: Converting 15% to 0.15 was right, but then the student multiplied 0.15 by 15, reusing the percent number instead of the base. The word 'of' points to the base, so it is 0.15 × 60 = 9.
onLevel.explanationEs: Convertir 15% en 0.15 estuvo bien, pero luego el estudiante multiplicó 0.15 por 15, usando otra vez el número del porcentaje en lugar de la base. La palabra 'de' señala la base, así que es 0.15 × 60 = 9.

extending.title: Find the Percent Error
extending.correctWork: 30% = 0.30 (divide by 100, not by 10). 0.30 × 90 = 27. The correct answer is 27.
hints: To convert a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 — how many places does the decimal move?
30% = 0.30, not 3.0. The student divided by 10 instead of 100.
extending.explanation: The conversion step is where it goes wrong: the student moved the decimal only one place and wrote 30% = 3.0. A percent is divided by 100, which moves the decimal two places, so 30% = 0.30 and 0.30 × 90 = 27.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de la conversión es donde falla: el estudiante movió el punto decimal solo un lugar y escribió 30% = 3.0. Un porcentaje se divide entre 100, lo que mueve el punto dos lugares, así que 30% = 0.30 y 0.30 × 90 = 27.

extending.prompt: A class has 32 students. 25% are in the math club, 50% are in the reading club, and 12.5% are in both. How many students are in each group? Can the total of all three groups be more than 32? Explain why or why not.
extending.sentenceFrame: There are ___ in math club, ___ in reading club, and ___ in both. The total ___ be more than 32 because ___.
extending.hint: Find how many students ARE in at least one club, then subtract from the total to find how many are NOT in either club.
hints: There are three separate percents of the SAME 32 students: 25%, 50%, and 12.5%. Find each group first.
Use friendly fractions: 25% = 1/4, 50% = 1/2, and 12.5% = 1/8. Then think about students who got counted in two groups.
Start with 25% of 32: that's 32 ÷ 4. Then do 32 ÷ 2 and 32 ÷ 8, and think about the 'both clubs' overlap.
extending.explanation: Taking each percent of the same 32 students gives 25% = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 in math club, 50% = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 in reading club, and 12.5% = 32 ÷ 8 = 4 in both. Adding 8 + 16 + 4 = 28 is misleading, because the 4 students in both are already inside the 8 and the 16 — counting them a third time overlaps, and the number of different students in at least one club is 8 + 16 − 4 = 20.
extending.explanationEs: Al tomar cada porcentaje de los mismos 32 estudiantes se obtiene 25% = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 en el club de matemáticas, 50% = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 en el club de lectura y 12.5% = 32 ÷ 8 = 4 en ambos. Sumar 8 + 16 + 4 = 28 engaña, porque los 4 estudiantes que están en ambos ya están incluidos dentro de los 8 y de los 16; contarlos otra vez los repite, y la cantidad de estudiantes distintos que están en al menos un club es 8 + 16 − 4 = 20.
extending.promptEs: Un salón tiene 32 estudiantes. El 25% está en el club de matemáticas, el 50% está en el club de lectura y el 12.5% está en los dos. ¿Cuántos estudiantes hay en cada grupo? ¿Puede el total de los tres grupos ser más de 32? Explica por qué sí o por qué no.
hintsEs: Hay tres porcentajes distintos de los MISMOS 32 estudiantes: 25%, 50% y 12.5%. Halla primero cada grupo.
Usa fracciones amigables: 25% = 1/4, 50% = 1/2 y 12.5% = 1/8. Luego piensa en los estudiantes contados en dos grupos.
Empieza con el 25% de 32: eso es 32 ÷ 4. Luego haz 32 ÷ 2 y 32 ÷ 8, y piensa en el traslape de 'ambos clubes'.

extending.instructions: A video game character starts with 500 health points. Complete the table to find how many health points are lost or gained.
hints: Watch the words 'of current' — each row uses the health from the row above it, not the original 500.
For each event: percent → decimal, multiply by the CURRENT health, then add (gain) or subtract (loss).
The potion row starts at 400 health. Find 50% of 400 (0.50 × 400) and ADD it since it's a gain.
extending.explanation: Each percent applies to the health the character has at that moment, not to the original 500. After the hit, health is 400, so the potion gives 400 × 0.50 = 200 gained for 600 health, and the poison then takes 600 × 0.10 = 60 lost, leaving 540.
extending.explanationEs: Cada porcentaje se aplica a la salud que el personaje tiene en ese momento, no a los 500 originales. Después del golpe la salud es 400, así que la poción da 400 × 0.50 = 200 ganados y llega a 600 de salud, y luego el veneno quita 600 × 0.10 = 60 perdidos, dejando 540.
extending.instructionsEs: El personaje de un videojuego empieza con 500 puntos de vida. Completa la tabla para encontrar cuántos puntos de vida pierde o gana.
hintsEs: Fíjate en las palabras 'del actual': cada fila usa la salud de la fila anterior, no los 500 originales.
Para cada evento: porcentaje → decimal, multiplica por la salud ACTUAL y luego suma (ganancia) o resta (pérdida).
La fila de la poción empieza con 400 de salud. Halla el 50% de 400 (0.50 × 400) y SÚMALO porque es una ganancia.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Find the Percent of a Number is multiplying by the percent number itself instead of its decimal form — for example, finding 30% of 80 by computing 30 × 80 = 2,400 instead of 0.30 × 80 = 24. Always divide the percent by 100 to get the decimal, then multiply that decimal by the base.

diagram.title: 12% of 1,500 Tickets Donated
diagram.caption: Each bar is a percent of the 1,500 tickets; 10% is 150, so 12% must be a bit more — 180 tickets, not 18.

connect.scenario: The arcade is donating 12% of Saturday's ticket sales to charity. They sold 1,500 tickets on Saturday. The manager says they will donate 180 tickets. A student says it should be 18 tickets.
connect.promptQuestion: Who is correct, and how do you know?
connect.prompt: The ___ is correct because 12% of 1,500 = ___ × 1,500 = ___. The mistake was ___.

exitTicket.explanation: 45% = 0.45. Multiply: 0.45 × 360 = 162. A student who answers 45 wrote the percent number itself instead of finding the part. A student who answers 315 subtracted the percent number from the base (360 − 45) instead of multiplying. A student who answers 180 rounded 45% up to 50% before multiplying (0.50 × 360). Always convert the exact percent to a decimal, then multiply by the base.
choiceFeedback: Multiply 360 by 0.45 to find 45% of 360.
Find 45% by converting to a decimal and multiplying.
Check: 45% = 0.45, then multiply by 360.
hints: You want 45% OF 360 — a part of 360, so the answer must be less than 360 but not tiny.
Convert 45% to a decimal, then multiply by the base: Part = Percent × Base.
Set up 0.45 × 360. (Shortcut check: 10% of 360 is 36, so 45% is 4.5 of those 36's.)

questions.stem: What is 200% written as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 200% ÷ 100 = 2.0. Percents greater than 100% become decimals greater than 1.

questions.stem: Which of the following is greater than 100%?
questions.explanation: 1.25 = 125%, which is greater than 100%. The other values are all less than 1 (less than 100%).
0.75% is less than 1%. All the other choices are greater than 1%.

questions.stem: What is 0.5% written as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 0.5% ÷ 100 = 0.005. Move the decimal two places to the left.
